mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to tightened discount rates reducing present value of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (current value + 0.25%) in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior month's average (p > 0.05) despite FEDFUNDS increase.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment) of at least 2% is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days, reflecting optimism about labor market strength and corporate optimism.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > (current value * 1.02) in the following month
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day average (p > 0.05) during qualifying PAYEMS jumps.

mechanism_narrative: When both HOUST (industrial production) and GDPC1 (goods orders) exceed their prior month's values simultaneously, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is predicted to be positive, indicating robust demand for capital goods.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > previous GDPC1 AND HOUST > previous HOUST
failure_condition: No statistically significant positive return in 20 days after qualifying dual series expansion (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of 3% or more predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days, as it signals supply-side weakness and potential market uncertainty.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < (current value * 0.97) in the following month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during qualifying INDPRO drops.

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained 3-month decline in CPIAUCSL (inflation), the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive as investors anticipate lower future rate hikes and improved earnings prospects.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreasing trend for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return during inflation decline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment) falls below 4.0% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is predicted to be positive, reflecting labor market tightness and investor confidence.
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly higher than prior 30-day average (p > 0.05) during qualifying UNRATE declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both RSAFS (retail sales) and HOUST (industrial production) by at least 5% in the following month predicts a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return, indicating broad economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > (current value * 1.05) AND HOUST > (current value * 1.05) in the next month
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 20 days after qualifying dual series surge (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When a 4% drop in FEDFUNDS occurs over the next quarter, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to the negative present-value effect of higher discount rates on future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < (current value * 0.96) over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 60-day returns not significantly lower than baseline (p > 0.05) during qualifying FEDFUNDS decline.
